messages:
Priya (support): Hey team, just got an escalation from Acme: p99 latency jumped from ~700ms to 5-8s for a subset of requests starting ~2026-03-15T10:40Z. Customer provided request IDs: req_8f7a, req_8f7b. They see a lot of backend queuing and occasional 429s. Can we triage? :eyes:

Ben (eng-runtime): Noted. Do we have tenant ID and model? Priya, can you paste the raw curl and one example response?

Priya (support): Tenant: acme-inc, model: rwd-3b-std, sample curl they ran:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"input":"status check","tenant":"acme-inc","request_id":"req_8f7a"}'
```

Response snippets from their side: many requests delayed ~5-8s, some returned 429 with body {"error":"admission_rejected","reason":"max_concurrency"}.

Ethan (oncall): ops-bot fired alerts around 10:39 UTC: high queue depth on runtime-pool-17 and sustained worker CPU at 95%. Suspect admission controller is tripping and piling requests.

ops-bot: [ALERT] 10:39 UTC runtime-pool-17 queue_depth=182, p99_latency(60m)=5200ms, admit_rejects=78

Lee (eng-sre): Copying logs now. Quick checks I'd run:
- confirm the pool (runtime-pool-17) hosts and autoscale status
- tail model server logs for OOMs or long GC pauses
- check KV cache hit rates (could cause CPU spikes if cold)

Ben (eng-runtime): Priya, can you reproduce internally with a burst runner against acme-inc tenant? If not, we'll simulate same QPS and payload shape. Also, what's their traffic pattern? bursty or steady?

Maya (customer-success): Acme says it started after a scheduled marketing campaign spike ~10:30 UTC, lots of short prompts with ~200-300 token outputs. Bursty, lots of concurrent workers hitting same model.

Lee (eng-sre): I ran quick probe:
```text
$ k get pods -n runtime | grep pool-17
runtime-17-a   2/2 Running   0     3d
runtime-17-b   2/2 Running   0     1d
runtime-17-c   1/2 CrashLoop  5     4h
```
crashloop seems related to a new quantized kernel load failure on one host, causes occasional fallback and short CPU spikes while reloading. That would cause queueing on remaining healthy replicas.

Ben (eng-runtime): That explains it. Fallback kernel reloads can spike latency and reduce effective concurrency. Two actions: immediate mitigations + followup. Immediate: temporarily pin acme-inc to a compatible model variant (rwd-3b-compat) on pool-18 that has stable kernels, and raise admission limit for that tenant by +30% for 20 minutes. Also enable quick fallback route to smaller model for non-critical requests.

Ethan (oncall): I'll take the hot path. Plan:
1) Increase tenant concurrency cap: 
```bash
# runtime admin
post /admin/tenants/acme-inc/concurrency 
body: {"delta": 30}"
```
2) Re-route 25% of traffic from pool-17 -> pool-18 by adding a temporary routing rule with weight 0.25
3) Restart the crashlooping pod after inspecting crash logs

Lee (eng-sre): Crash log shows: 
```text
error: failed to load kernel "attn_v3_q8": checksum mismatch, fallback to generic kernel
stack: ...
```
Suggest we cordon that host from serving the quantized variant until we patch.

Priya (support): I pushed the actions to the playbook and informed Acme we're doing a soft split and temporary cap bump. They want ETA to restore p99 < 1s.

Ben (eng-runtime): Also flip on prefix KV cache warmup for acme-inc (they're bursty, cache coldness hurts). Small script to warm cache with recent prompt signatures.

Ethan (oncall): Executed steps:
- increased concurrency cap for acme-inc by 30% at 10:51 UTC
- added routing rule: pool-18 weight 0.25 at 10:52 UTC
- cordoned host host-42 (where crashlooping pod ran) at 10:54 UTC
- restarted runtime-17-c after addressing temp file permissions at 10:56 UTC

Lee (eng-sre): Metric snapshots after interventions (10:57 UTC): p95 dropped from 1.8s -> 340ms, p99 dropped from 5.6s -> 820ms, admit_rejects down from 78 -> 3 in last 5m. Queue depth now ~14.

Priya (support): Acme confirms their end: p99 is back under 1s for most flows, they see a few straggler tasks but overall OK. :thumbsup:

Maya (customer-success): I'll schedule a call with Acme to review root cause and offer a credit. Also recommend we follow up on the host/kernel issue.

Ben (eng-runtime): Follow-ups for engineering:
- infra: mark host-42 for kernel image rollback / repro and ensure quantized kernel checksum pipeline includes stronger validation.
- runtime: add better gradual kernel reload (throttle reloads per host) and circuit-breaker so a single crash doesn't spike CPU for others.
- platform: improve tenant overload protection UX (auto-suggest route fallback to smaller model).

Lee (eng-sre): Creating a postmortem ticket: P-176890-acme-queueing. I'll include timeline, actions, and metrics. Also will add an alert to detect repeated kernel fallback events (>=3 in 10m) so we can auto-schedule host draining.

Priya (support): Thanks all. I'll close the customer escalation once postmortem and credit are confirmed. Leaving thread for any follow-ups.

Ben (eng-runtime): Nice fast work. Leaving a TODO: add a replay test that simulates kernel-fallback + burst to catch this before customer impact.

ops-bot: [INFO] Incident ticket created: P-176890-acme-queueing

Ethan (oncall): Any objections to leaving the routing rule for 2 hours and then auto-rollback? If not, I'll set the rollback timer.

Maya (customer-success): Fine by me, keep me posted before rollback.

Lee (eng-sre): No objections. I'll follow up with host remediation plan in the ticket.

Priya (support): Resolving on our side. Will post postmortem link here when ready.

(Reaction summary: many :thumbsup: and :eyes: across replies)
